articles.title: Ubisoft Almost Made a Zelda Game With Ganondorf as the Protagonist
articles.summary: Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history.
articles.body:
Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history.

Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson says the project was internally titled Goliath, so as to appropriately echo the size and scale of what Ubisoft Milan hoped to achieve with the game. It was an ambitious plan, and one that former Ubisoft developer Gian Marco Zanna described as a “new big bang in the video game universe.”

This description, while dramatic, is accurate; Ubisoft Milan’s Zelda game would have been drastically different from anything we’ve seen from the series thus far. Rather than following Link’s adventures in the wilds of Hyrule, it would have been a spin-off title in the broader Zelda universe featuring a brand-new, “never-before-seen character.”

60 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Screenshots

However, during its early concept phase, Nintendo reportedly asked that this protagonist be changed to the franchise’s ultimate big bad: Ganondorf. This would have been the first time Ganondorf was the central, playable character in a Zelda game, and on paper, it sounds like a fantastic idea… but unfortunately, it didn’t end up coming to fruition.

Sources told Henderson that Ubisoft Milan was given a deadline of late 2023 to come up with a prototype for this Ganondorf game, but Nintendo reportedly rejected their proposal when the time came, for reasons that have not been made clear.

Ubisoft Milan was behind the highly-lauded Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, which IGN scored a sparkling nine out of 10 . The studio reportedly began ideation for Goliath shortly after its release, clearly riding the high of its successful launch. It’s almost painful to imagine the game we could’ve had; perhaps it was a Ganon origin story?

Given that it was a spin-off and not a sequel or prequel, it’s unclear what, exactly, Ganon would be doing in this game. And what about Ubisoft Milan’s first intended protagonist for the project?

We have so many questions, and it’s likely that none of them will ever get answered. Ubisoft did not respond to Henderson’s requests for comment, but he did note that it had internally acknowledged a journalist requesting information about Goliath beforehand.

Among the oodles of canceled, top-secret games over the years, this one definitely makes us go down the ‘what if’ rabbit hole. It’s almost as tantalizing as the canceled Disney Smash Bros.-style game , which former concept artist Ken Christiansen shared artwork for on his personal online portfolio, showing characters like Captain Hook, the Sheriff of Nottingham, the Queen of Hearts, John Silver, and others facing off in 2v2 battles.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: The Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop Drops to $1,449 During Walmart's GeForce Week Sale
articles.summary: Strong gaming chops in a slim and lightweight chassis.
articles.body:
Walmart's GeForce Week Sale is ending soon, but there's still time to pick up a great deal on a powerful gaming laptop. For a limited time, Walmart has the Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop for just $1,449.00 with free shipping. In addition to the powerful GPU, the A16 Pro comes preinstalled with 32GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD, which means you don't need to go out and pay an exorbitant amount of money to add more.

Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop for $1,449

Gigabyte A16 Pro 16" Intel Core i7 240H RTX 5070 Ti Gaming Laptop (32GB/1TB)

The Gigabyte A16 Pro laptop measures 0.77" at its thinnest point and weighs just 5 pounds, which is light for a 16" gaming laptop. It's equipped with a 16" 2560x1600 165Hz IPS display, Intel Core 7 240H CPU, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12GB GPU with 115W TGP, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The Intel Core 7 240H is a 10-core CPU with a max turbo frequency of 5.2GHz. This is a solid, efficient processor for gaming. The RAM is not user upgradeable so it's good that the system already includes 32GB pre-installed. The SSD, on the other hand, is user-upgradeable.

The GeForce RTX 5070 Ti mobile GPU can handle the most demanding games

The RTX 5070 Ti mobile GPU performs about 20%-30% better than the RTX 5070. Compared to Nvidia's previous generation RTX 4000 mobile GPUs, it's comparable in performance to the RTX 4080 and pulls ahead of it in games that support DLSS 4.5 and multi-frame generation. The A16 Pro's 5070 Ti GPU is throttled down to 115W TGP instead of the usual 140W max in order to cut down on heat, but it's powerful enough to run most games smoothly on the display's 1600p resolution from classic favs like League of Legends, Roblox, or Fortnite to new releases like Onimusha: Way of the Sword .

articles.title: PlayStation Reportedly Polling Game Developers After Decision to Kill Discs Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: PlayStation is reportedly sending a lengthy survey to game developers with a question about how they sell physical games after their decision to stop producing physical game discs prompted intense backlash.
articles.body:
PlayStation is reportedly sending a lengthy survey to game developers with a question about how they sell physical games after their decision to stop producing physical game discs prompted intense backlash.

The death of physical discs will not happen quietly; fans are making their voices heard as loudly as possible, to the point where PlayStation itself is reportedly reaching out to game developers asking for their thoughts on the divisive subject.

Speaking on the Broken Silicon Podcast , content creator, writer, and showrunner Tom claimed that he’d been made aware of a survey making the rounds among game developers from Sony. His sources claimed that it was possibly the longest survey that Sony has ever distributed.

GTA 6 Special Edition PlayStation 5 DualSense Wireless Controller

“There is a survey Sony sent out to developers that is, what I was told by my contacts, a bigger survey than they’ve sent almost ever before, if not ever before. And there was a question in it basically trying to ask in a not-direct way, ‘Is there an issue with how we sell games physically?’ or something, like asking developers for feedback on killing discs.

“ Wolverine is still selling plenty of physical copies, and you’ve also got Sony starting to ask devs if they are worried about killing physical [discs], suggesting they realize that if they got a bunch of feedback, maybe they would consider some sort of mea culpa on it. We’ll see.”

As noted by Destructoid , this claim comes on the heels of multiple reports from gamescom that developers at the event were expressing severe displeasure at Sony’s choice to forgo physical games. While it’s best to take Tom’s specific claims of a survey with a grain of salt for now, it wouldn’t come as a surprise if Sony were really testing the waters after hearing such strong feedback.

However, executives at the company have made it clear that they don’t plan on pulling back from their all-digital future; in a July investor Q&A, chief financial officer Lin Tao confirmed that Sony is going to proceed in spite of the backlash.

“We have received various opinions and people have strong views, and we understand that the community has put forth those views to us. Games are loved by many people. It’s a form of entertainment that’s loved by people, and it’s connected to people’s fond memories in many cases,” she said through a translator.

“And so we understand those emotions. We want to consider that. And in the future digital ecosystem, how do we engage the gamers is something that we would like to continue to explore.”

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom Video Review - IGN
articles.summary: Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom reviewed by Len Hafer on PC."It's been a long wait for any new single-player RTS stories in the Warcraft universe. And while it's hard to say a drought that long was worth it, I'm not at all displeased with what we got in the end. I would have loved more RTS-style missions in Forsaken Kingdom, but the deeper RPG mechanics and a story that fits right into the Warcraft 3 era seamlessly kept me hooked to the end. Definitive Edition is now for sure my favorite graphical style of the ones available – if only it were available for the old campaigns, which I still love to replay every few years. And a new multiplayer hero has made the ladder feel dynamic and interesting again in a big, visible way."

articles.title: Ebon Moss-Bachrach in Final Talks for Heat 2 Role
articles.summary: Michael Mann’s Heat 2 is set to start shooting in November, with The Bear's Ebon Moss-Bachrach in final talks to play Kelso, previously portrayed by Tom Noonan.
articles.body:
The Bear’s Ebon Moss-Bachrach is reportedly in final talks to join Michael Mann’s Heat 2 as Kelso, according to TheWrap . Kelso is the mysterious former DARPA researcher and hacker who furnishes Neil McCauley character with the intel he needs to take down his scores. Kelso was played by Tom Noonan in the 1995 original. Noonan passed away earlier this year, in February .

The two-time Emmy winner will join a stacked cast, including Leonardo DiCaprio as Chris Shiherlis (originally played by Val Kilmer), Christian Bale as Detective Vincent Hanna (originally played by Al Pacino), and Stephen Graham in Robert De Niro’s old role as Neil McCauley.

Shooting is reportedly scheduled to begin in November.

Heat 2, which was first released as a novel by Mann and thriller author Meg Gardiner in 2022, serves as both a prequel and a sequel to the events of the original film, which is widely considered to be one of the greatest heist films of all time. Mann has wanted to turn Heat 2 into a movie for some time , resolving in 2023 that he was planning for the project to be his next film .

While the original film was made with Warner Bros., Heat 2 has since ended up at Amazon MGM Studios.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

articles.title: Forza Horizon 6 Dev Responds to 'Itasha' Car Ban Backlash, Says 'Explicit Sexual Content' or 'Sexually Suggestive Content' Is Forbidden
articles.summary: Over the last few months, Forza Horizon 6 has received an outpouring of negative comments on social media and Steam about the game’s moderating system, which has been perceived as unfairly targeting players who create Itasha-style designs. To address this, Microsoft recently released an updated code of conduct in an attempt to clarify what kind of user generated content will get players banned in Forza Horizon 6.
articles.body:
Over the last few months, Forza Horizon 6 has received an outpouring of negative comments on social media and Steam about the game’s moderating system, which has been perceived as unfairly targeting players who create Itasha-style designs. To address this, Microsoft recently released an updated code of conduct in an attempt to clarify what kind of user generated content will get players banned in Forza Horizon 6.

Itasha (literally “painful car,” for their bold appearance that can be cringeworthy to some) are custom-decorated cars often featuring characters from manga, anime, and video games. This real-life phenomenon that started in Japan has gathered a following, with players showing off their love for certain characters in car games like Forza Horizon 6, which allow players to extensively customize their vehicles with vinyl decorations. However, it seems that not all Itasha creators have been able to enjoy sharing and racing their designs across Forza 6’s Japan setting.

Over the last few months, there has been an increase in comments online from users alleging that there has been a huge wave of bans across Forza 6. Many posts allege that Itasha have been unfairly targeted and urge people not to purchase the game: “If you love Japanese car culture, don’t buy it. You’ll regret it.” This has fuelled discussions (like this one on Reddit ) and speculation that AI moderators are being used, and that certain groups are mass reporting certain designs or creators. Such comments have also stoked fears that even having a screenshot of another player’s Itasha or having a draft livery design sitting in your library could result in a permaban.

To address these speculations, Forza Motorsport developer Turn 10 Studios ( which Microsoft recently merged with Horizon developer Playground as part of an Xbox studios shakeup ) clarified in its latest updated guidelines that each piece of reported content is checked by human moderators. “Once content has been flagged using the in-game reporting system, the content is added to a queue to be reviewed by a human moderator. The number of reports on a piece of content does not affect its prioritization or position in the queue.”

Turn 10 also addressed Itasha designs specifically in its updated guidelines on specific iconography and imagery:

“Itasha style designs are permitted; however explicit sexual content and sexually suggestive content are forbidden. While we cannot show specific examples of suggestive imagery in this article, designs that depict provocative poses, associated gestures and facial expressions, and attention to specific body parts can be examples of suggestive imagery.”

However, these updated guidelines are already facing criticism online. “These criteria are too vague,” chimed in one Japanese-language commenter on X . “Seriously, it’s just the same as saying ‘whatever I think is bad is bad!’”

“At least there are some specific examples and descriptions,” another commenter posted in Japanese. “Well, I guess I poses (standing on one leg with the other leg up) and M poses (legs parted) would be out. I guess they want to say ‘keep it within the bounds of what’s okay for kids to see,’ but due to the political correctness in British criteria, it’s damn hard to understand these judgments.”

According to Forza 6’s policy, players are usually given a warning for their first violation, with any additional violations after that receiving increasingly long suspensions. However, if a player’s behavior or custom design falls within the zero tolerance policy, they end up permabanned: “Only when an image contains child sexual content, explicit sexual content, explicit nudity, or imagery outlined above in Forza's Zero Tolerance Policy, will a permanent ban be issued without prior infractions.”

Extreme violations cover “offenses that Turn 10 has ZERO tolerance for, including hate speech, credible violent threats, child sexual exploitive (sic) abusive imagery, terrorism or violent extremism content, sexual/nude imagery, and more.”

Female characters on Itasha are sometimes put in poses that might be deemed too sexually suggestive to pass Forza 6’s guidelines. The perceived age of anime characters can also be an issue that might prompt such censorship (as seen in Steam’s 2018 crackdown on anime-style adult games ). These factors may have nudged some of these Itasha creations into Forza 6’s Zero Tolerance Policy, which results in a permanent suspension.

Over on Steam, Forza Horizon 6’s Japanese review status has plunged to “Mixed,” with a recent increase in Japanese language reviews not recommending the game. Some players describe the risk of getting permabanned just for taking a screenshot of another player’s car that violated regulations, alleging that car designs featuring female anime characters wearing bikinis have also been banned. Even positive reviews that describe the game as “great fun just to drive around as you can freely explore a miniature version of Japan,” describe the operational side of the online game as “extremely poor quality,” also highlighting issues with season missions and collecting credits. “I find myself wondering if they couldn’t be a bit more considerate towards their users, as it is far from a cheap game. Given that the game itself is of such high quality, I feel it's a great shame that its reputation is being undermined by these issues.”

Overall, the perception seems to be that Forza Horizon 6 has been stricter with its bans than previous titles in the series, and there still remains much concern over what and what doesn’t constitute bannable content.

While some commenters writing in Japanese on social media were angry at the banning of Japan’s imperial flag , it is worth noting that these iconography bans are hardly a new development unique to Forza 6. Previous entries in the Forza franchise also banned such imagery (including the Confederate flag and Nazi iconography). For example, back in 2020, former Forza creative director Mike Brown talked about Forza 4’s moderating system and how accurate depictions of Japan’s Imperial flag on car designs could get a player banned, but more abstract expressions would not. These same guidelines regarding Japanese imperial flag usage were reposted in Forza 6’s September 24, 2026 guidelines regarding specific iconography that is banned.

When Forza Horizon 6 was released, it received initial praise across Japanese social media for respecting Japanese culture and giving players a realistic-looking mini-version of the country to race around. However, it remains to be seen if Turn 10 can win back the vocal community complaining about its moderation system.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

articles.title: 'That's Where Doomsday is Born': Avengers Director Discusses Endgame Encore's New Ending That Rewrites Steve Rogers' Story
articles.summary: Avengers: Endgame director Anthony Russo has discussed the movie's newly-extended final scene, and how it leads directly into Avengers: Doomsday.
articles.body:
Avengers: Endgame director Anthony Russo has discussed the movie's newly-extended final scene, and how it leads directly into Avengers: Doomsda y .

Speaking during a Q&A after a New York screening of Avengers: Endgame Encore, Russo was asked about moments in the film which are designed to take on a fresh meaning or significance now, with Doomsday in the pipeline.

Warning! Spoilers for Avengers: Endgame Encore follow...

Perhaps unsurprisingly, Russo pointed to Endgame Encore's big finale twist, which sees Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter's happy ending suddenly interrupted by a visit from Loki. As revealed yesterday by fans who attended early showings , Steve and Peggy's romantic dance together does not last long. This new version of the scene sees Loki drop by, seemingly from his tenure as a TVA agent.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

"There's certainly a pivotal moment at the end where... the moment has a different meaning," Russo teased (via Avengers Updates ). "We play one beat past where Steve Rogers' story ended with Peggy Carter, and in that moment, that's where Doomsday is born."

While Russo did not elaborate further, the suggestion here is that whatever Steve, Peggy, and Loki decide sets in motion the eventual rise of Doctor Doom — and fans have certainly got theories. In a recent teaser, we saw Doom mourning his wife and child, and fans believe that whatever timeline shenanigans Steve and co. get up to, their actions inadvertently set Doom on a path of revenge.

There's lots here that we don't know, such as why Loki needs to visit Steve in the first place, and where the former Captain America ends up. Fans have posited that Steve and Peggy are actually being saved by Loki from living in a universe that will soon be destroyed, and wind up in Doctor Doom's universe instead. Other speculation points to issues caused by Steve and Peggy ultimately having a child there — in a reality they don't belong — somehow removing another child to balance the multiverse's scales.

Of course, we don't have long to wait to find out the answers to these questions. Avengers: Doomsday will arrive in theaters on December 18, and pick up Steve Rogers' story from there. Here's hoping everything goes absolutely fine for him and his family, and nothing bad happens at all. Yep.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Woot's New Sale Includes the Best Switch 2 Console Deal of the Year, But it Expires Today
articles.summary: Woot's new 'Fall in Love with Video Games' sale includes the best Switch 2 console deal of the year so far, but it expires before the end of the day (September 25, 2026).
articles.body:
Amazon-owned Woot has just kicked off its brand-new 'Fall in Love with Video Games' sale , and there's a surprisingly decent line-up for those looking to save a little extra, a little early.

While the next Amazon Prime member exclusive sale is coming up soon on October 6-7 , alongside the big ol' sale season fast approaching with Black Friday and the rest, you might be more inclined to just wait out sales like this and look out for even better deals in the coming months. It's a wise choice, and one I'll never judge.

I still want to highlight a couple of decent deals from this Woot sale that I wouldn't expect to see again soon. Or, at least, they won't get any better than this.

Nintendo Switch 2 Console (Grade A Refurbished)

The big highlight from the sale will undoubtedly be the Nintendo Switch 2 consoles. Nintendo has recently upped the price of these bad boys to $499.99 in the US, but you can actually pick up the console for just $389 instead. There are a couple of hoops you need to jump through, but for $110 in savings, it might be worth it.

Before the hoops, I will caveat by saying this is a 'Grade A Refurbished' Nintendo Switch 2, not new. In this economy, I wouldn't turn my nose up at refurb deals, as this is an almighty good offering for a console that is essentially as good as new.

To qualify for the deal, you'll need to shop the sale via the Woot app , which will grant you an additional 20% off the current list price. That brings it down to $409, $90 in savings, and a pretty great deal to start with. But if you've never shopped with Woot before, then you're in luck, as this will bag you an additional $20 off, bringing it down to $389, as I mentioned. No promo code required either, as the discount will be applied automatically at checkout.

articles.title: Nintendo Wins $4.5 Million From Reddit Mod Who Sold Pirated Switch Games
articles.summary: Nintendo has finally won its long-running lawsuit against a reddit moderator who sold pirated Switch games, and been awarded $4.5 million in damages.
articles.body:
Nintendo has finally won its long-running lawsuit against a reddit moderator who sold pirated Switch games, and been awarded $4.5 million in damages.

We've been tracking Nintendo of America's legal action against James "Archbox" Williams for the past two years, ever since the firm initially used a combination of reddit posts and Williams' own Nintendo repair orders to track him down and launch litigation back in late 2014.

Williams was accused of leading the reddit community SwitchPirates, whose 190,000 members regularly discussed how to download illegally pirated games and circumvent Nintendo's anti-piracy measures. Williams was also accused of operating and advertising various online "shops" where piracy-enabling software and tools could be acquired.

Nintendo initially demanded $4.5 million from Williams last year , though said at the time that this figure was "nowhere near an amount that would compensate Nintendo of America for the seriousness of the Defendant's conduct." Almost 12 months later, the full amount has now been awarded by default — seemingly because Williams did not respond to the lawsuit at any point.

"It is ordered and adjudged that default judgment is hereby entered against Defendant James C. Williams," reads a ruling filed this week, confirming that Nintendo of America has now been awarded the $4.5 million it previously demanded, as well as a permanent injunction barring Williams from selling pirated Switch games and other piracy-assisting software or modded consoles.

Williams must now close all of his remaining online "shops" where "extensive libraries of pirated Nintendo Switch games" have been made available for download, and any social media accounts, Discord servers and the like where these have been advertised.

The legal victory follows another big win for Nintendo in Europe earlier this month , where the Mario maker successfully had the sale of piracy-enabling Switch accessories banned from sale. Commonly marketed as the MIG Switch, these devices can circumvent Nintendo's anti-piracy measures and play illegal copies of games downloaded from the internet. Nintendo made headlines last year after it began penalizing players who had used these devices on their consoles , disabling the machines' online functionality.

This is, of course, far from the first time that Nintendo has initiated legal action to stop the sale of piracy-enabling devices. Last year, a Nintendo console modder who refused to shut down his business — and who then attempted to defend himself without a lawyer — was ordered to pay $2 million by Nintendo . And then there's the infamous case of Gary Bowser, an employee of a company that sold anti-piracy devices, who served time in jail and was ordered to pay $14.5m in damages, a debt he's said he will now repay for the rest of his life .

Now, Nintendo just needs to track down Archbox and get him to pay... We'll keep an eye on how all that goes, and keep you updated.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: The Next Halo Game From Halo Studios Was Reportedly Still Years Away, Before Microsoft Handed the Franchise to Activision
articles.summary: The next Halo game from Halo Studios was reportedly still years away from launch before Microsoft canceled it this week.
articles.body:
The next Halo game from Halo Studios was reportedly still years away from launch before Microsoft canceled it this week.

Microsoft continued its Xbox "reset" this week by gutting Halo Studios, leaving a skeleton crew to manage existing games in the series, and handing the Halo franchise to Call of Duty company Activision . Activision is setting up a new team to build the next mainline Halo game, leaving what remains of Halo Studios out of the picture.

Microsoft also moved Sea of Thieves developer Rare and Age of Empires developer World's Edge under the Activision umbrella as part of the studio shakeup. It made a very different call with the troubled Halo Studios, however, which has seen multiple Halo projects canceled.

According to The Verge , the next game under Halo Studios was years away from shipping, “so Microsoft pulled the plug instead.” The last mainline Halo game, Halo Infinite, launched nearly five years ago, in December 2021.

Halo Studios has endured a tumultous time in recent years, with significant leadership changes sparking questions about the future of the company and its games. Staff affected by this week's layoffs have spoken out across social media this week. One former employee took to LinkedIn to say: “I'm a jumble of thoughts and emotions, but mostly relief. I was miserable for the last year and a half and it'll be nice to feel something different.”

Microsoft obtained Halo when it acquired its original developer, Bungie, in 2000. After helping establish the Xbox console with Halo and Halo 2, Bungie split from Microsoft to become independent again in 2007. It went on to work on looter shooter Destiny as part of a high-profile, 10-year publishing deal with Activision. Meanwhile, Microsoft set up 343 Industries, so named after 343 Guilty Spark from the Halo games, to take Halo into a new era.

2012's Halo 4 was the first Halo game released by 343. It was followed by 2015's Halo 5: Guardians, which in turn was followed by 2021's much-delayed Halo Infinite. Halo Infinite in particular struggled, and this year's Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the beloved first Halo game, suffered problems of its own .

In 2024, 343 Industries changed its name to Halo Studios and announced plans to work on multiple new Halo games that would all be developed on Epic's Unreal Engine. The announcements were unveiled in a seven-minute video shown ahead of the Halo World Championship's grand finals, which showcased the results of Project Foundry — an experimental project designed to show a Halo game built using Unreal Engine. While it was not much more than a tech demo, the video offered a glimpse at a fresh beginning for Xbox's flagship franchise in the wake of Halo Infinite's troubled launch.

Questions remain over what Activision plans to do with Halo now it’s in charge of its fate. Microsoft has said it’s setting up “a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty.” Microsoft has yet to say when the next Halo game will come out, or if Activision plans to reboot the series or rotate it into its schedule of releases for Call of Duty, which hasn’t missed an annual release for 20 years.

Rob Kostich, president of Activision issued the following statement:

"We’re thrilled to welcome Halo, Rare, and World’s Edge to Activision. It’s an honor and a responsibility that we do not take lightly. These teams and their games have inspired fans around the world for decades.

"For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place. It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.

"To the World’s Edge and Rare teams, we can’t wait to get to work together."

New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is looking to double down on the company's biggest franchises, such as Fallout, Minecraft, and Halo, and release big new games in those franchises more frequently. Activision releases a brand new, mainline Call of Duty game ever year. Sharma may be hoping some of that rubs off on Halo.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: 'I've Made a Living Out of Misbehavior': The First Trailer for Johnny Depp Movie Day Drinker Seems to Include Some Knowing Nods to His Career Revival
articles.summary: A first trailer for Johnny Depp's upcoming movie Day Drinker seems to include several knowing nods at the star's bid for career revival.
articles.body:
A first trailer for Johnny Depp's upcoming movie Day Drinker seems to include several knowing nods at the star's bid for career revival.

Due in 2027, Day Drinker is Depp's second upcoming project to be backed by a major studio, following hot on the heels of Ebeneezer, a starry retelling of Charles Dickens classic A Christmas Carol that arrives in theaters this November.

While Depp has been busy with a few smaller projects, the Pirates of the Caribbean star has not appeared in a mainstream Hollywood movie for years, following a series of high-profile legal battles with his ex-wife Amber Heard.

Now, however, Depp appears to be mounting a comeback, via movies which feel well chosen for his current status. In Ebeneezer, Depp will play a hated figure who learns the error of his ways and ultimately ends up beloved by all. And in this first look at Day Drinker, Depp plays a mysterious alcoholic who seems to become entangled with the law while helping expose a criminal operation.

"I've made a living out of misbehaviour," Depp's character says in the trailer as he's cuffed and forced to the ground, before he affords the camera a little smile. "I see no tangible reason to stop now. Don't you sometimes want to misbehave?

"My story? Perhaps it's a tale of revenge," Depp's character continues, apparently in an Irish accent. "Or perhaps something worse. What if all this is a ghost story? Or maybe I'm just another day drinker."

"You thought I was f***ing done?" he concludes at the trailer's end. "I'm done when I say I'm done."

Pirates of the Caribbean Movies in Order

Day Drinker stars Depp as the eponymous alcoholic, alongside Madelyn Cline and Penelope Cruz. Noteworthy talent behind the camera includes The Amazing Spider-Man director Marc Webb (looking for his own comeback after helming Disney's widely-panned live-action Snow White), and Fast X co-writer Zach Dean. The movie is currently set to launch on March 26, 2027.

One of the big questions surrounding Depp is whether he'd return for a potential new Pirates of the Caribbean movie. Last month, Pirates of the Caribbean producer Jerry Bruckheimer reignited hope of Depp reprising his iconic role as Captain Jack Sparrow one more time while issuing a fresh update on Disney's long-in-development plans for Pirates of the Caribbean 6 . Bruckheimer confirmed that conversations were underway with Depp for the actor to potentially return as the infamous pirate.

Bruckheimer has long expressed interest in Depp donning his Captain Jack Sparrow costume once again , even when it seemed unlikely , as Disney mulled other, alternative routes forward for the franchise. Depp's past legal issues with Heard saw Disney largely distance itself from the star, leading to some choice words from Depp in response . Meanwhile, long-gestating plans have placed Barbie star Margot Robbie at the forefront of Pirates 6 if and when it does ever materialize.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Bungie Says Marathon Flopped Because It Was Too Hard
articles.summary: Bungie has admitted that extraction shooter Marathon failed at launch because it was too hard to attract a mainstream audience.
articles.body:
Bungie has admitted that extraction shooter Marathon failed at launch because it was too hard to attract a mainstream audience.

Marathon was designed as an ultra hardcore PvPvE extraction shooter where repeated death was built into the risk / reward game loop. If you die, you lose all your gear. And not just what you looted while out on the battlefield, but what you brought in. And given how easy it was to die in Marathon, particularly in PvP situations, it could feel like a brutally punishing video game.

Players certainly noticed this and made their feelings clear, even before Marathon launched. At the time, Bungie responded to concerns about its steep, unwelcoming learning curve to say that while the game was a “dangerous climb,” its difficulty could be overcome. The Sony-owned studio tried to make the point that players should play the long game, slowly improving their base stats and gaining access to better items by completing contracts and progressing faction upgrades. But unfortunately for Bungie, many players were immediately put off by the constant failure they experienced simply trying to get to grips with the game. The release of brutally difficult and complex endgame raid, Cryo Archive, in April only doubled down on the sense that Marathon was built for only the most hardcore of shooter fans.

Even former professional Counter-Strike player, Shroud, expressed concern about Marathon’s difficulty, saying that while Cryo Archive offered an incredible experience, it was too hard for casual players. "Cryo Archive is insane,” he said in April. “It's the most elaborate extraction shooter map I've ever seen in a game ever. The loop that they made is truly something special. The problem is, is it too elaborate? Is it too complex? Is it too much of a grind? Is your 9-5 grandma and grandpa going to be able to do it? I don't know."

Now, in detailing radical changes coming to Marathon as part of Bungie’s bid to save the game, developers have talked about what went wrong.

“Launch didn’t go the way we wanted it to,” Kevin Yanes, senior design lead, said in a new video. “We all built a game that we believed would resonate. But I think when you’re so close to something it’s hard to see the bigger picture objectively. And so we made a game that was overly difficult I think for a lot of folks. And that constant loop of failure I don’t think spoke to as many people as we hoped it would.

“While death is the first step for many players, death was the only step.”

Game director Del Chafe III called out Marathon’s PvP, which he called “sweaty.”

“One of the things we learned at launch is that our game is pretty niche,” he said. “It’s for sweaty people who like PvP. And, to be fair, a lot of us on the team like those experiences.”

“We all thought we were gonna bring extractions to the masses, and we didn’t, right?” Yanes added. “We built very much an extraction shooter as it was, as you’ve ever seen one.”

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

The question now for Bungie and for Sony is, how can the developers turn Marathon around? Certainly part of the plan is to make it more accessible, but adding dedicated PvE modes is the key. Bungie will also add a team deathmatch mode, and expand Perimeter, essentially its tutorial level, to be closer in scope to other full zones.

Bungie's goal seems to be limiting the friction that new players feel and letting them filter themselves into more familiar gameplay types. That should, in theory, let people ease themselves into the traditional extraction mode that's proven so divisive.

The changes to Marathon were revealed in the same breath as Bungie announced a surprise return to the world of Destiny 2. Having initially ditched the game, Bungie will now unvault content, although it is not returning to full live service support . Bungie has said it’s got more Destiny in its future, though. What this turns out to be remains to be seen.

Last week, Bungie denied a rumor that it planned to merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs amid continued questions about the future of both franchises. Based on this week’s news, the plan is to soldier on with Marathon, at least into 2027. The spectre in all this is of course Sony’s ongoing commitment to Marathon. It has backed the game publicly, but some fans are worried about its future. Steam concurrents do not paint the full picture of a multiplatform game, but it’s worth noting that Marathon had a 24-hour peak of 3,285 on Valve’s platform, down from an all-time peak of 88,337 set when the game launched in March.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: The Best Weird-But-Great Steam Games of the Year (So Far)
articles.body:
If there’s one thing Steam excels at it’s being a gold mine of weird and wonderful games. Of course, it has all the big blockbusters too, but if you take the time to dig a little deeper you’ll find all kinds of obscure treasures that, in my opinion, are just as much fun to play as the games your mates are always blabbering on about.

It’s not always easy finding those curios though, which is where the Steam Hype Playlist comes in. Every month it focuses on a different part of Steam to uncover the hidden gems you’ve likely never heard of, and this time we’re looking at 10 of our favourite oddball picks of 2026.

This is the closest you’ll find to mainstream here and it’s one of Steam’s highest-rated games so far this year. Creature Kitchen is short, sweet and a fantastic concept: living alone in a haunted cabin in the woods, you are menaced by eyes in the darkness, cryptids and creatures lurking in the shadows, who happen to be so very hungry. So obviously you hit the cookbooks, rustle up dinner and voila, you have new friends! Despite its creepy setting there are no jump-scares and no pressure, just a casual cooking experience that benefits from pure low-fi charm and whimsical writing.

Long-awaited after a hugely successful Kickstarter, Endacopia is a gem of an old-school point-and-click adventure. Part whimsical comedy (inspired by kids' edutainment games like the Putt Putt series), part unsettling horror, you can never be sure what it's going to hit you with next. Balancing tension with gags, whimsy, jump scares, and some great musical numbers, it’s relatively short – around 6-7 hours if you love adventure games – but there's enough secrets and non-linearity to give it rare replay value in a genre not known for it. Those who really dig deep will be rewarded by a hidden optional ending that’s well worth sticking around for.

Developer/Publisher: Crayon & Kit/The Crayon Eating Company

Genre: Kleptomaniac Collectathon Platformer

Funi Raccoon Game is absolute, gleeful chaos in videogame form. You are a horrible raccoon on a quest to collect one of every object in the world for your ever-expanding dumpster home. Part dreamlike exploration adventure (think Yume Nikki), part breakneck, unhinged platformer, its world is almost entirely built out of stock 3D and 2D art assets smashed together haphazardly, so it looks really distinctive. It's consistently hilarious too, with a story that has some sharply critical things to say, especially in the back half of the game, but it never strays too far away from the screwball comedy.

Genre: Genre-hopping Magical Misadventure

A short but oh-so-sweet narrative adventure with a ton of endings and secrets to discover. After developing magical powers and accidentally setting your apartment on fire, you seek the help of a local Witch's coven to help control your skills. Unfortunately, the only person around is Mesmer, a terrifyingly chaotic yet weirdly likeable young witch with unusual speech patterns, who will come to your aid if you help her complete a ritual she's been working on. Prepare to roll back the clock and explore alternate paths to unravel the truth as the game hops between genres and minigames, making sure that you’ll never be doing one thing for long.

Developer/Publisher: Cadence Petersen & Hazel Fackler

Pronoun Palace is a sharp, satirical and painfully funny word-puzzle roguelike. Your pronouns have been confiscated by the government for being too disruptive, sending you on a quest to fight for them.You do this using a grid of Scrabble-style tiles, spelling words to attack – the more obscure letters you use, the more damage you deal. Each enemy has their own gimmicks: one might force you to use certain tiles, others might make some off-limits, while some reshape the board itself. It has fantastic music, smart art, and funny writing, and is a puzzle game you absolutely should check out.

Genre: Extremely Normal Horse Betting Simulator

The smartest dumb game (or dumbest smart game?) you'll play this year. Breed and race wobbly low-fi horses to raise enough money to cure your partner's Horse Flu. But doing it properly takes time and luck, so you might want to cut some corners by heading down to the shady research lab to gene-splice your nags (with every gene being fully simulated) to make them super powered. Or, y’know, just cross-breed them with trucks. If you let loose one of your prize mutants, their genes spread into the ecosystem, making the whole world and the horses you’re racing against even weirder still. Every playthrough is different, every player has their own approach, and every run is packed with painfully funny moments.

Developer/Publisher: Nathan Grange, Léonard Lemaitre & Niels Tiercelin/IronEqual

You’ve been running for hours through impossible structures populated by strange naked people-things that talk to you about the importance of filing your paperwork properly. Vholume is a dream-like (nightmarish?) parkour experience, with you sprinting, wall-running and butt-sliding through the narrow alleys and crumbling tunnels of an impossibly vast concrete megastructure. There's something hazy and surreal about both the aesthetics and feel of the movement here, making it very easy to get into a focused flow state, aided further by a dreamy, ambient synth soundtrack. Lots of secrets hidden in this one too, and the community-made levels are already piling up.

Developer/Publisher: Grey Alien Games & Night Signal Entertainment

Genre: Haunted Horror Solitaire Dungeon Crawl

You’ve found a rare copy of an obscure horror-themed card game that made headlines back in the ’90s. Obviously, the correct thing to do is explore its depths, even as people mail you increasingly worrying news clippings about people dying unexpectedly after playing the game. It’s a fantastic mix of retro creepypasta-style horror, tongue-in-cheek humour, and genuinely smart solitaire gameplay, with a complex magic system to master and even turn-based stealth segments played entirely with cards. The patched-in New Game+ mode, with new levels and puzzles for players with a fully powered-up character, means there’s tons to do too!

Before Dishonored and Prey, Arkane gave us Dark Messiah of Might & Magic, a rough-edged but action-packed take on the immersive sim genre that provided a world full of precarious ledges to cast slippery ice spells on and pointy spike traps to punt orcs into. The Adventures of Sir Kicksalot is a tribute that fully embraces the silliness of Dark Messiah’s funniest moments. Kick people into the ocean, sneak around wearing a barrel, snack on bananas to create traps for enemies.... There’s so much to do and it’s a big ol’ laugh.

Developer/Publisher: Recurring Dream/Outersloth & Indienova

A mystery-filled puzzle box, part haunted computer adventure, part traditional point-and-click puzzler, and all a test of how computer literate you are. You’ll be picking through directory trees, poring through .TXT files and using smartly overlapping desktop applications to reveal hidden data as you search for secrets within an old computer your character inherited from their uncle. Not to spoil too much about the game, but it swerves into more traditional point-and-click adventure territory as you progress, unveiling extremely haunted games within less haunted games.

And that’s all we’ve got time for here, but there’s so much more to see, with our Steam Hype Playlists covering nine titles every month from the start of this year. Want more deep cuts like this? Just looking for someone to help you filter out the gems from Steam’s never-ending firehose of releases? That’s exactly what we do over on Steam Hype , the latest site on the Hookshot network.

articles.title: How Barnes & Noble Laid the Foundation for a Toys 'R' Us Comeback
articles.body:
I used to love going to Toys 'R' Us as a kid. It wasn't just the new toy that I inevitably came home with that I enjoyed; it was the experience of browsing a bunch of cool stuff in person. So I was absolutely thrilled by the news that the iconic toy store is making a comeback after closing the last of its brick-and-mortar stores back in 2018. The convenience of shopping online is in part what killed the toy store in the first place, but cultural trends are starting to shift as folks seek out real-life retail experiences once again.

I can't help but look at the incredible recovery of Barnes & Noble to explain why a Toys 'R' Us comeback makes a lot of sense in 2026.

If you've been to a Barnes & Noble recently, you've certainly noticed that it isn't just a place to buy books anymore — nor has it been since 2019 when the company started focusing on curated experiences. There are Starbucks cafés mixed with reading lounges and themed gifts stashed in little pockets all over these stores now. The most relevant newer addition — and a sign that a Toys 'R' Us comeback makes sense — is the massive toys and games section in many locations.

While Barnes & Noble is still primarily a bookstore, it has become something more by focusing on elevating the retail experience to compete in a digital economy. "I think a proper bookstore has to be curated, and that is the essence of one of the core skills of what it is to be a bookseller,” said Barnes & Noble CEO James DGaunt in a 2024 interview with CNN . “You are trying to have the titles that you think will most interest your customers and display them. The sensible thing to do is just have fun in each individual store.”

This approach is in direct opposition to Amazon's own physical bookstore efforts that launched in 2015, which focused primarily on a "ratings-first" approach to stocking books that mirrored its online store. Amazon ended up closing all of its physical bookstores back in 2022 . As someone who frequented my local Amazon bookstore, it isn’t hard to see why it failed as a concept. While there were some cool sectionst to browse, the layout of the store felt like it was designed to sell you Echo devices and bestsellers only. There wasn’t much thought put into the feeling of discovery as you browsed.

And that's really the key to what Barnes & Noble has been able to achieve. The stores have been redesigned into a third space where people can feel comfortable hanging out and discover something new. It's the type of positive experience that makes you want to buy something, rather than feeling obligated to buy just because you entered the store.

Toys ‘R’ Us has clearly taken a page from the Barnes & Noble playbook in this way. The official press release about the Toys 'R' Us comeback even made a point to focus on the idea of this experience: "Select locations will introduce new experiences at the intersection of play, entertainment and content creation, including Creator Studios, dedicated spaces where influencers, creators and toy brands can create content, unveil new products and host toy reveals, launches and special events. Select stores will also feature candy shops and cafés, giving customers even more reasons to explore, discover and spend time at Toys 'R' Us."

Even the addition of “Creator Studios” feels like a step away from what Barnes & Noble has been doing for years with author signings and readings. It makes a trip to your local store more than just a shopping trip. It’s an actual event where you can leave feeling like you were part of something bigger than the toy you bought.

Kids Aren't the Only Target Market Anymore

While Barnes & Noble established the foundation for what a successful brick-and-mortar store can look like in 2026, it's success isn’t the only reason Toys 'R' Us is attempting a comeback. The reality is that the toy market isn't just about kids anymore; it's about adults too. Toys 'R' Us kids have grown up and now have disposable income to spend on things they like, which is sometimes a lot of cool LEGO sets, collectibles, and trading card games.

According to recent Circana research , "The toy industry's growth continues to be fueled increasingly by older consumers,” noting that adult-only households accounted for 55% of toy sales, making them the largest contributor to the industry overall.

With adults as a growing target market, Toys 'R' Us stores have the opportunity to attract a much larger share of the market than before. There will still be a focus on toys specifically for kids, sure, but you'll also likely find a thriving Pokémon TCG market and quite a few 18+ LEGO sets featured prominently throughout the stores when they launch this holiday season.

Looking at the success of Barnes & Noble over the last few years, it’s definitely easy to see how a more curated approach could lead to a successful Toys ‘R’ Us relaunch. This is especially true if you consider the fact that the company is planning on opening all of these new stores during the holiday season. Black Friday and Christmas are two of the biggest times of year for toy sales, and Toys ‘R’ Us will undoubtedly succeed by resurfacing during this key window of time. It feels eerily similar to how Spirit Halloween has approached the month of October every year.

The real question is, how will the company keep up the momentum after the holiday season? The toy industry may be seeing an influx in adult audiences, but that doesn’t mean they will be willing to make the trek to Toys ‘R’ Us every month. With Amazon able to offer inevitably lower prices on most of the products the company is able to sell, they will need to double down on the in-person shopping experience to keep those new stores open beyond 2026.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: Blizzard Insists Actual Humans Are Reading Through All the WoW Forever Beta Character Names It Banned Players for This Week
articles.summary: Blizzard is banning players who it feels have created highly offensive character names in the World of Warcraft: Forever beta, and warned fans against “testing” the system.
articles.body:
Blizzard is banning players who it feels have created highly offensive character names in the World of Warcraft: Forever beta, and warned fans against “testing” the system.

While Forever, a new version of World of Warcraft that’s meant to act as a sort of “Classic+” experience, doesn’t launch until November 4, the beta was made available last week and it was immediately flooded by players . One of the new features in the game is dual names, so you can have a first and second name for your character. This opened the floodgates to some hilarious character names, but also some that crossed Blizzard’s line.

In a post on the Blizzard forum , the company issued a no-nonsense warning to forever beta players, saying actual humans were looking at character names to ban those it considers to be out of line.

“We are in the process of issuing forced name changes to characters found to be in violation of our character naming policies that were created in the Forever Beta,” Blizzard said. “Additionally, we have removed beta access for some users who created names that were far outside of our Code of Conduct. The use of dual names has allowed players new levels of creativity and personalization with your characters, some took this opportunity to reveal too much about themselves and will no longer be participating in this Beta.

“The World of Warcraft team takes the safety and inclusiveness of our game very seriously. These actions were performed directly by the World of Warcraft Development team and were individually reviewed. The Customer Service team cannot and will not assist with any appeals. Our system for enforcing naming standards will be coming online very shortly, we would appreciate testers refraining from 'testing' this system, as you run the risk of being actioned and losing access to the Beta. Please keep your character names respectful and within policy.”

This week, some players took to social media to complain that they had been unfairly booted out of the beta due to their character names, and questioned whether humans were behind the decisions. “My name is Devil Tootsalot,” said one player . “How is that highly offensive? Are you guys auto-moderating this? There is no way a human banned my name.”

But senior game producer Tom Ellis defended Blizzard’s tough stance here, tweeting to say players were probably banned because of a character they created but aren’t necessarily playing.

“Anyone saying they were removed from beta for naming their character ‘Billy Mcsuckmahballz’ is telling little white lies,” Ellis insisted. “That character likely just received a forced name change.

“Multiple unfortunate humans read through every name that was removed from beta today. If you’re genuinely confused, remember that it’s our database, we can see every character you’ve created, not just the one you’re playing.

“I read the list. No sympathy. Be a better human next time.”

Creating funny names for World of Warcraft has been a community tradition ever since the game launched over 20 years ago, and Blizzard has also had to work to prevent genuinely offensive names over that time period, too. But with the launch of Forever, Blizzard now faces an influx of potentially problematic character names all over again as players rekindle memories of World of Warcraft back in 2004 and 2005. The question is, will Blizzard be able to keep up with the huge number of launch players the popularity of the beta suggests is coming its way?

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.
